assertion: Desktop real and mobile stub modules retain explicit platform support and sealing status.
Model-root resolution must not fall back to cwd and must retain existing asset provenance.
Fixed model URLs and digests are preserved without authorizing download.
Exists-only Ready status is not verified model integrity or successful load.
Automatic status/listener hookup is distinct from download and is covered by the sealed entry map.
Switching downloads cannot let an old task mutate the new generation's status or file.
Connect/total timeout do not supply a byte/disk budget for model responses.
Opening a partial model truncates it; progress emit is not persisted successful download.
Abort plus best-effort partial deletion does not prove the old task released the path.
Digest/flush/rename publication has explicit existing-target and platform failure behavior.
Removing a model file does not cancel transcription already holding its Arc context.
Direct permission command and start-triggered macOS prompt are independently sealed.
Non-macOS permission true does not certify actual device/OS permission.
Listening means stream-play readiness, not transcript completion or durable capture.
Reaching the sample cap does not itself stop the microphone stream.
Capture error, stop signal and async Idle update are not one atomic event.
Stop returns Processing before transcription and must not imply transcript delivery.
Cached model context must be bound to asset identity rather than only model ID.
Cancel in Processing suppresses output but does not necessarily interrupt blocking CPU work.
Listening cancel reports stop/join failures instead of treating Idle state as shutdown evidence.
Emitted transcript plus ephemeral React ID is not a durable Session-bound Delivery.
Key release before slow permission/start cannot leave unexpected active capture after the grace window.
Swallowed shortcut rejection and failed event emit require a diagnosable non-success state.
Registered commands, hooks and enabled shortcuts mean source-active until code sealing is actually tested.
Supported scope/kind combinations remain explicit; workspace config is rejected rather than silently redirected.
Global public file editing must not silently use the provider's CODEX_HOME as product authority.
Strict workspace AGENTS checks cover existing and dangling symlinks plus replacement races.
Intentional global AGENTS external-symlink compatibility is explicitly distinguished from root containment.
Global config strict symlink policy must also reject a dangling external target before write.
Unbounded read_to_end and always-false truncation require explicit size and partial-response semantics.
Direct write failure may truncate or partially change the file and is not atomic replacement.
File read/write target the daemon host in remote mode and must display that authority.
Arbitrary export requires a verified user-selected target, not merely a nonempty path argument.
Remote/mobile image command still reads locally; machine identity cannot be inferred from mode alone.
Image normalization/encoding leaves Codex module ownership without losing format and size safeguards.
Five native config cross-writes and app settings save have independent partial-success outcomes.
All twelve clipboard callers retain content-specific privacy and failure handling.
Code-block HTTP links and ordinary HTTP/HTTPS/mailto links have distinct scheme and callback rules.
File URL, relative, absolute and mounted-path links do not implicitly authorize external roots.
Selected external-app preference is stored before execution and is not rolled back on open failure.
Provider auth URL is sensitive and does not become a public arbitrary-URL executor.
Dialog selection/confirmation is not server-side permission or durable Owner authorization.
Each menu action reaches its actual callback; popup construction alone is not a mutation result.
Native menu show/focus/emit failures are not successful user-visible navigation.
Check-update menu remains linked to network/cache writers.
Platform quit/close/hide paths keep different host-lifecycle contracts.
Tray labels and raw IDs cross the main-window boundary and require privacy scope.
Tray-open-thread revalidates the public target rather than trusting an old raw native ID.
Settings persistence and actual native theme application have independent error states.
Single-instance focus does not forward the second instance's arguments or cwd.
Pinned window-state plugin persistence needs its own observed root/format before migration.
Linux environment, macOS lifecycle, Windows chrome and iOS insets require separate platform evidence.
